thread:
mike: Quick heads-up — planned control-plane config migration scheduled Thu 2026-03-19 02:00-02:45 UTC. Expected symptoms: short routing flaps, occasional 503s for <~15s, and warmup latency spikes for a few minutes after. No long-term degradation expected. Posting ops play, status-page text, and a customer email draft below. Please review and flag any regulatory/customer blockers.

jess: @mike thanks — ETA on total blackout vs degraded perf? I want to make sure oncall knows SLO thresholds. Also please confirm if Dedicated customers should be notified separately.

mike: Good call. No full blackout expected — mostly transient 5–15s errors as control-plane nodes rotate. We'll mark Hosted as 'degraded performance' and set a scheduled maintenance window on status. Dedicated customers get targeted email (legal/compliance earlier).

incidents-bot: /status create draft saved as "maintenance-controlplane-2026-03-19" — use /status publish <id> to post. Reminder: scheduled updates can auto-notify subscribers.

sara: Copy. I'll coordinate Dedicated list export and send targeted email. @nate can you help with the canary routing policy during the window?

nate: On it. Plan: enable route-fallback to eu-west-primary for 10% of warmup traffic, keep request retries at 2, and raise alert thresholds on API-5xx. I'll push a short Runbook snippet to the oncall channel before handoff.

mike: Ops play (short):
1) Pre-window (30m): export customer list, snapshot control-plane state, create status draft, notify support rotations.
2) Start window: set status -> "degraded performance" and pin message on support channel. Apply config migration to control-plane group A.
3) Monitor: tracing + per-region token-latency dashboards, API-5xx alert. If >5% 5xx sustained for 2m, abort and rollback.
4) Post-window (15m): bump status to "maintenance — complete" then back to "operational" after 30m stability. Post short postmortem stub.

Status page draft (paste this into StatusPage):
```
component: Production API (Hosted)
status: degraded_performance
scheduled_for: 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z
expected_duration: 45 minutes
notes: "We will be performing a control-plane configuration migration. During the maintenance window you may observe brief request errors (5xx) and temporary latency increases. We will monitor closely and roll back if we observe sustained errors."
```

Customer email draft (Hosted customers):
"Hello — We will be performing a short maintenance on Thu, Mar 19, 02:00–02:45 UTC that may cause brief request errors or increased latency. We do not expect prolonged outages; however if you rely on high-availability SLAs and expect impact please reply and we will coordinate. — Redwood Inference Ops"

Customer email draft (Dedicated customers):
"Hi — As part of routine maintenance in our control plane, we're scheduling a configuration update on Thu, Mar 19, 02:00–02:45 UTC. We expect no SLA impact but are sending this advanced notice. If you have specific maintenance windows we should avoid, please reply. — Redwood Inference Support"

jess: Nice. Two asks: 1) add a short canned internal Slack blurb for Support to paste, and 2) can we have an oncall handoff note? I can take handoff at 01:45 UTC.

mike: Support canned blurb (copyable):
"We're performing a control-plane migration (2026-03-19 02:00–02:45 UTC). You may see brief errors and latency spikes. Please triage per Runbook 'control-plane-migration-v2' and escalate to eng-oncall if >5% 5xx sustained for 2m. Status updates on https://status.redwood.ai."

mike: Oncall handoff: jess will be primary from 01:45–04:00 UTC. Nate will be secondary. Post handoff + ping in #eng-oncall with link to status draft. I'll be on standby.

incidents-bot: scheduled status update created: maintenance-controlplane-2026-03-19 (will publish at 2026-03-19T01:50:00Z unless canceled).

sara: Sending Dedicated email batch at 01:30 UTC. Support blurb posted to #support at 01:40 UTC.

nate: Quick checklist I'm adding to the runbook before handoff:
- confirm routing fallback toggled
- watch API-5xx and token-latency dashboards
- keep retrier set to 2 so we don't amplify errors
- verify K8s rollout freezes for non-control-plane jobs
- rollback helm chart tag ready (tag v2-rollout-prev)

jess: Got it. I'll post real-time updates in this thread during the window. If anyone wants to join the bridge, I'll open one at start. :phone:

--- 2026-03-19 02:18 UTC (during window) ---

jess: Update: applied migration to group A at 02:06. Seeing short 5xx bursts ~8s, spiking to 4% for ~30s, then back to <1%. Continuing with group B.

nate: Rolling group B now, fallback policy active for 10% traffic. Watching dashboards.

incidents-bot: StatusPage update: published (maintenance-controlplane-2026-03-19) — link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/maintenance-controlplane-2026-03-19

mike: If we see sustained >5% 5xx for 2m, rollback. We're under threshold so continuing. Great coordination so far.

--- 2026-03-19 02:41 UTC (post-window) ---

jess: Migration complete at 02:39. Observed a 2–3m warmup with higher latency, now stable. Marking window as complete in StatusPage and sending final customer note.

incidents-bot: StatusPage update: maintenance complete.

mike: Final customer note (send):
"Maintenance complete — The control-plane configuration migration has finished as of 2026-03-19 02:39 UTC. Some customers may have seen brief errors or latency spikes; services are now operational and stable. If you continue to see issues please contact support@redwood.ai. — Redwood Inference"

sara: Dedicated customers notified with the 'complete' email at 02:45 UTC. Support thread closed at 03:10 after no open escalations.

nate: Postmortem stub created: owner @mike, timeline + metrics attached. Will expand into a full postmortem if any customer-impacting regression is found.

jess: Thanks everyone — smooth run. Leaving notes in the runbook and closing out. :thumbsup:

mike: Huge thanks to the oncall and support teams. I'll file the short ops summary and link it to the scheduled postmortem.

"""
